findings.where: Motion specimen, the whole section at both widths: the full-width lilac panel behind 'Settled, unhurried, once.', the curve, the replayed line and the timing table
findings.fault: The motion section sits on a saturated lilac field. That colour is in none of the tile's palette, the house colours or the direction. When you squint below the fold it is the loudest block on the page and it outweighs the article specimen, so the tile ends looking like a different brand. Counsel's paper allows one soft ivory ground, blue and grey as the only ink, and pale yellow as the one colour memory. Lilac breaks all three, and it pulls a soft, playful tone into a page meant to read as a lawyer's paper.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether v1 holds to 'one soft ground at low contrast, the house blue and grey as the only ink' and 'refined, never childish'. Mark too: he likes the blue and grey, and a lilac band reads as neither legal nor his.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download', and the bold article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law'
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide black grotesque, a third face that is not part of the type pair. The type pair names Newsreader 500 for subheads and Public Sans for labels. Inside a quiet serif article these heavy sans blocks are the darkest marks on the screen and they jump out ahead of the text they introduce. The article title is also set much heavier than the light line the tile is built on. Together they make the reading page loud and blunt rather than a journal's calm gravitas, and they don't show the type pair the specimen claims to prove.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff reading Mark's article, who expect a measured legal voice and get headings that shout. The founder too: the brief says 'serious type' and 'nothing reads as in-your-face', and asks the article specimen to show the look surviving Angélique's subheads.

findings.where: Whole page: the hero at both widths, and the Texture specimen's half-width yellow bar
findings.fault: The direction's one colour memory, pale legal yellow behind one quotation or the contact panel, appears nowhere on the page as a visitor sees it. It shows only as a swatch and as a sliver in the texture diagram. The brief also allows it behind a quotation, so this does not depend on the contact strip. Without it the first screen is grey type on ivory beside a portrait. That is calm, but it is a look any consultancy could own, and it isn't the 'legal pad saved with careful intention' that this direction exists to test.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first and asked for the legal pad to be saved deliberately and for the look to be 'alive, not boring'. With the pad's one trace missing, they can't judge v1's lever.

findings.where: Hero, first screen at both widths: the supporting paragraph under Mark's line
findings.fault: The first screen says what Mark does and for whom, but not where. Nothing names the regions or countries of his work, though the brief gives his talks in Melbourne, Istanbul and São Paulo. A visitor can't tell from the hero whether he has worked in their region.
findings.who_objects: Staff at multilateral development banks, who shortlist advisors on relevant region and project kind. First-visit trust items 2 and 6 ask an international advisor to show the regions of his work.

findings.where: End of the article specimen into the Motion section: the 'Download' row ('Streamlining the PPP Process…' and 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'), at both widths
findings.fault: The download row sits almost touching the lilac motion panel. On the phone the 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' line butts straight onto it. Every other section break on the page has generous space. So by proximity the download reads as the top of the motion section rather than the end of the article, and the article ends without a pause.
findings.who_objects: The founder, scanning the specimens as separate parts, who sees the article's last item run into an unrelated block. The brief calls the PDF list 'the product', so it should close the article clearly.

findings.where: Palette specimen: the four swatches (square paper, rounded grey, ellipse blue, slightly rounded yellow)
findings.fault: The four swatches in one row take four different shapes, and the blue one is an ellipse. By similarity the eye reads the shape as meaning something, as if blue were a different kind of thing from the other colours, when the shapes mean nothing. The ellipse is the odd one out and reads as a stray button or badge.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the palette to see four colours on equal terms, who is left wondering what the ellipse is meant to signal.
